items.title: Getting started
items.description: Add EDS to a React, Bootstrap, or Venom project and give agents the same reference.

sections.title: Quick start with AI
sections.body: Paste this into your coding agent. It installs EDS and writes version-matched project guidance without replacing your instructions.
sections.code: Install @edmunds/eds-core, @edmunds/eds-theme-edmunds, @edmunds/eds-bootstrap-adapter, and @edmunds/eds-cli. Run `eds init`, then read the managed EDS block in AGENTS.md.

sections.title: Install
sections.body: Install the component package, Edmunds theme, Bootstrap compatibility layer, and CLI.

sections.title: Add CSS in contract order
sections.body: The bridge imports Bootstrap and EDS into explicit cascade layers. App utilities and overrides remain above the system.
sections.code:
@layer reset, bootstrap, eds-foundations, eds-components, app-utilities, app-overrides;
@import "@edmunds/eds-bootstrap-adapter/bootstrap-bridge.css";

sections.title: Add your first component
sections.body: Use per-component entry points so imports remain predictable for people, bundlers, and agents.

sections.title: Explore
sections.body: Use the CLI before authoring a screen: inspect a related template, then retrieve each component contract.
sections.code:
eds template --list
eds template inventory-results --skeleton
eds component VehicleCard --dense
eds golden VehicleCard
eds docs tokens

sections.title: Open the living artifacts
sections.body: design-system.html is the portable visual contract and embeds the current registry. scratchpad.html is a throwaway interactive surface for resolving ambiguous design decisions before product integration.

items.dense: Install core/theme/bootstrap-adapter/cli; run eds init; import bridge CSS; use per-component imports; inspect templates then component docs.

items.title: Principles
items.description: The product promises that guide EDS decisions.

sections.title: Comparable by default
sections.body: Vehicle identity, price, mileage, and dealer facts occupy consistent positions so shoppers can compare without relearning the interface.

sections.title: Guidance over lock-in
sections.body: EDS owns accessible behavior and semantic APIs. Teams retain controlled composition and documented CSS escape hatches.

sections.title: One reference
sections.body: The website, Figma mapping, CLI, agent files, and MCP are generated from the installed component and token contracts.

sections.title: Earned by use
sections.body: A component becomes stable only after real product use, accessibility review, and human plus agent evaluation.

items.dense: Principles: comparable by default; guidance over lock-in; one generated reference; stability earned through use and evaluation.

items.title: Design tokens
items.description: DTCG primitives and semantic roles shared by code and Figma.

sections.title: Use semantic roles
sections.body: Build product UI with surface, text, action, status, price, and border roles. Primitive ramps are inputs to the theme rather than app-level choices.

sections.title: Generated outputs
sections.body: One token source produces CSS custom properties, TypeScript, Bootstrap Sass variables, registry data, and Figma Variables.

sections.title: Modes
sections.body: Light is the default. Dark and high-contrast modes override semantic roles without changing component source.

items.dense: DTCG tokens generate CSS/TS/Sass/Figma. Apps use semantic --eds-* roles, not primitive colors. Modes override semantics.

items.title: Accessibility
items.description: WCAG 2.2 AA behavior is part of every stable component contract.

sections.title: Native first
sections.body: Prefer native controls and landmarks. Custom behavior must preserve semantics, accessible names, focus order, and keyboard operation.

sections.title: State is communicated
sections.body: Loading, error, selected, expanded, and saved states are exposed programmatically and never rely on color alone.

sections.title: Release gate
sections.body: Stable components require automated axe coverage, keyboard scenarios, zoom and reduced-motion review, and manual assistive-technology checks.

items.dense: WCAG 2.2 AA: native first; expose all states; stable requires axe, keyboard, zoom, reduced motion, and manual AT review.

items.title: Working with AI
items.description: Make agents retrieve installed EDS contracts before generating UI.

sections.title: Required workflow
sections.body: Search templates, inspect the closest skeleton, then retrieve documentation for every component used.

sections.title: Dense output
sections.body: All read commands accept --dense for a compact, version-specific contract that fits agent context windows.

sections.title: Golden examples
sections.body: Use `eds golden <Name>` as the primary composition reference after retrieving the component contract. Golden examples are generated from the same typed documentation.

sections.title: Interactive uncertainty
sections.body: When product intent is ambiguous, build the smallest option in scratchpad.html, state the decision being tested, and wait for approval before integrating it.

sections.title: Fail fast
sections.body: Run `pnpm lint:eds` before type checking. It rejects hardcoded colors, inline style objects, and direct React-Bootstrap or Bootstrap behavior imports in product and template source.

sections.title: MCP
sections.body: The authenticated MCP provides search and get over the same registry as the CLI and documentation portal.

items.dense: Agents: template --list; template NAME --skeleton; component NAME --dense; golden NAME. Ambiguity goes to scratchpad.html. Run lint:eds. MCP search/get serves the same registry.

items.title: Venom and Bootstrap migration
items.description: Introduce EDS one route at a time without changing product behavior.

sections.title: Layer first
sections.body: Load Bootstrap and EDS in explicit layers before replacing controls. Verify a smoke page with Button, TextField, Card, and VehicleCard.

sections.title: Migrate in product slices
sections.body: Apply tokens and shell, then replace shared controls and automotive compositions, then complete routes.

sections.title: Keep behavior intact
sections.body: Do not mix the visual migration with changes to routing, data fetching, analytics, SEO, or business rules.

items.dense: Venom migration: establish layers; smoke-test foundations; migrate shell then controls/patterns then routes; preserve business behavior.

items.name: Button
items.description: Button starts an immediate action such as saving a vehicle, applying a filter, or submitting a lead.
items.whenNotToUse: Use Link when the interaction only navigates to another location.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Shows progress and prevents duplicate activation.

props.name: onAction
props.description: Action callback with automatic async progress.

accessibility: Uses a native button and defaults type to button.
Async actions expose aria-busy and a polite loading announcement.
keyboard: Enter or Space activates the button.

bestPractices.description: Use one primary action per decision area.
Use a verb that names the result, such as Save vehicle.
Use destructive styling for reversible actions.

examples.name: Save vehicle
examples.description: Primary action on a vehicle card.

items.responsive: Labels remain visible. Use the sm size only in space-constrained toolbars.
items.dense: Button action trigger. import @edmunds/eds-core/Button. label required; variants primary|secondary|tertiary|destructive; async onAction manages loading.

items.name: TextField
items.description: TextField collects a short, free-form value with persistent labeling and validation.
items.whenNotToUse: Use Select when users must choose from a fixed set of valid values.

props.name: description
props.description: Help text announced with the field.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hides but preserves the label.

accessibility: Always renders a programmatically associated label.
Error and help text use aria-describedby.

bestPractices.description: Use a concise noun phrase for the label.
Explain how to resolve a validation error.
Use placeholder text as the only label.

examples.name: ZIP code
examples.description: Location input used in inventory search.

items.responsive: Expands to the width of its containing form region.
items.dense: TextField labeled text input. import @edmunds/eds-core/TextField. label required; description and errorMessage wire aria-describedby.

items.name: VehicleCard
items.description: VehicleCard presents a single inventory result with comparable pricing, mileage, location, and actions.
items.whenNotToUse: Use a data row for dense comparison tables or a media gallery on a vehicle detail page.
accessibility: Save uses a pressed-state button with a vehicle-specific name.
The heading gives each result an accessible landmark name.
keyboard: Tab reaches save and details actions in visual order.

bestPractices.description: Keep price, mileage, and location in consistent positions across results.
Use the dealer-provided image description when it adds useful context.
Mix financing qualification language into the primary price.

examples.name: Used SUV result
examples.description: Search result with deal rating and payment estimate.
examples.code: <VehicleCard year={2023} make="Honda" model="CR-V" trim="EX-L AWD" price={28990} mileage={18420} dealLabel="Great price" />

items.responsive: Media stays above content on narrow cards; search templates control column count.
items.dense: VehicleCard inventory result. import @edmunds/eds-patterns/VehicleCard. year/make/model/price required; save is aria-pressed; use in listing grids.
